nodes.name: Missing ownership check
nodes.description: Always check the `AccountInfo::owner` field of accounts that aren't supposed to be fully user-controlled.
nodes.fix: Create a helper function that takes an untrusted `AccountInfo`, checks the owner and returns an object of a different, trusted type.

nodes.name: Setting Associated Token Account as Owner
nodes.description: Setting an associated token account as the owner of a token account by mistake can lead to loss of control over the account.
preconditions: Passing an associated token account (ATA) as the owner when creating a new account
nodes.fix: Do not set an associated token account as the owner of another token account.

nodes.name: Improper Validation of Associated Token Account
nodes.description: Validating an associated token account only by its owner and mint is insufficient, as it may allow unexpected token accounts to pass.
preconditions: Using constraints like `vault_ata.owner == vault.key()` and `vault_ata.mint == vault.mint` without using `get_associated_token_address`
cfg_patterns: Validation without checking if the account is an ATA
nodes.fix: Use `get_associated_token_address` for validating associated token accounts.

nodes.name: Missing Signer Check
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not check if the authority account is a signer, allowing unauthorized accounts to execute the log_message instruction.
preconditions: The authority account in the LogMessage context is not checked for being a signer.
nodes.insecure_pattern: pub fn log_message(ctx: Context<LogMessage>) -> ProgramResult { msg!("GM {}", ctx.accounts.authority.key().to_string()); Ok(()) }
nodes.fix: pub fn log_message(ctx: Context<LogMessage>) -> ProgramResult { if !ctx.accounts.authority.is_signer { return Err(ProgramError::MissingRequiredSignature); } msg!("GM {}", ctx.accounts.authority.key().to_string()); Ok(()) }

nodes.name: Account Data Matching Vulnerability
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not verify that the authority matches the owner of the token account, allowing unauthorized access to the account balance.
preconditions: The `authority` is not checked against the `owner` of the `token` account.
nodes.fix: if ctx.accounts.authority.key != &token.owner { return Err(ProgramError::InvalidAccountData); }

nodes.name: Incorrect Authority Check
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not properly verify that the token account is owned by the SPL Token program.
preconditions: The `token` account is not checked to ensure it is owned by the SPL Token program.
nodes.fix: if ctx.accounts.token.owner != &spl_token::ID {

nodes.name: Missing Discriminant Check
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not check if the account data has a valid discriminant, which could lead to unauthorized access or manipulation.
preconditions: The `user` account is not checked for its discriminant.
nodes.fix: if user.discriminant != AccountDiscriminant::User { return Err(ProgramError::InvalidAccountData); }

nodes.name: Reinitialization Vulnerability
nodes.description: The insecure version allows reinitialization of an already initialized account without checking if the account is already initialized.
preconditions: The `user` account has been previously initialized.
nodes.fix: if !user.discriminator { return Err(ProgramError::InvalidAccountData); }

nodes.name: Arbitrary CPI to SPL Token Program
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program allows arbitrary cross-program invocations (CPI) to the SPL Token program without verifying that the provided token_program account is indeed the SPL Token program. This can lead to unauthorized operations if a malicious actor provides an incorrect or spoofed token_program account.
preconditions: The `token_program` account in the context is not verified against the known SPL Token program ID.
ast_patterns: solana_program::program::invoke without checking the program ID of the invoked program
cfg_patterns: transfer instruction called on an unverified token_program account
nodes.fix: if &spl_token::ID != ctx.accounts.token_program.key { return Err(ProgramError::IncorrectProgramId); }

nodes.name: Duplicate Mutable Accounts
nodes.description: The insecure version allows the same account to be passed twice as mutable, leading to potential unintended side effects or vulnerabilities.
preconditions: Same account is passed for both user_a and user_b
ast_patterns: Account<'info, User> without unique key constraint
cfg_patterns: update function without checking if user_a and user_b are the same
nodes.insecure_pattern: let user_a = &mut ctx.accounts.user_a; let user_b = &mut ctx.accounts.user_b;
nodes.fix: Add a check to ensure user_a and user_b have different keys.

nodes.name: Bump Seed Canonicalization Vulnerability
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not properly validate the bump seed, allowing an attacker to manipulate the derived address and potentially bypass intended access controls.
preconditions: The `set_value` function in the insecure version does not check if the provided bump matches the expected bump.
nodes.fix: let (address, expected_bump) = Pubkey::find_program_address(&[key.to_le_bytes().as_ref()], ctx.program_id);

nodes.name: Incorrect PDA Seeds in WithdrawTokens
nodes.description: The insecure version uses incorrect seeds for generating the Program Derived Address (PDA) when transferring tokens, which can lead to unauthorized token withdrawals.
preconditions: The `withdraw_tokens` function is called with an incorrect PDA seed.
ast_patterns: Incorrect seeds used in the `with_signer` method call.
cfg_patterns: Token transfer without proper signer check due to incorrect PDA seeds.
nodes.fix: let seeds = &[ctx.accounts.pool.withdraw_destination.as_ref(), &[ctx.accounts.pool.bump]];

nodes.name: Account Data Not Zeroed Out
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not zero out the account data when closing it, which can lead to sensitive information being left in the account's memory.
preconditions: The `close` function is called without zeroing out the account data.
nodes.fix: Zero out the account data before closing it.

nodes.name: Sysvar Address Checking Vulnerability
nodes.description: The insecure version of the program does not verify that the provided account is indeed a Rent sysvar, allowing an attacker to pass any arbitrary account and potentially bypass intended checks.
preconditions: The `rent` account in the context is not verified against the known Rent sysvar address.
ast_patterns: AccountInfo without explicit verification of sysvar ID
cfg_patterns: Function call to check_sysvar_address without sysvar address validation
nodes.fix: rent: Sysvar<'info, Rent>,

nodes.description: A malicious contract can repeatedly call a vulnerable function to drain funds.
preconditions: Function modifies state and transfers value

cfg_patterns: Multiple entry points for the same function
nodes.fix: Use checks-effects-interactions pattern; ensure proper reentrancy guards

nodes.name: Integer Overflows & Underflows
nodes.description: Rust, Solana's primary development language, prevents overflows in debug mode but defaults to two's complement wrapping in release mode. If developers do not proactively manage integer boundaries, this can lead to unintended behavior.
cfg_patterns: Use checked arithmetic operations to prevent overflows and underflows
nodes.fix: let result = a.checked_add(b).ok_or(ErrorCode::ArithmeticOverflow)?;

nodes.name: Precision Loss in Arithmetic Operations
nodes.description: Incorrect handling of decimal precision can result in rounding errors, affecting token balances or financial calculations. Developers should use fixed-point arithmetic where possible to minimize these issues.
preconditions: Decimal precision is not handled correctly
cfg_patterns: Use fixed-point arithmetic for precise calculations
nodes.fix: let result = (a * PRECISION) / b;

cfg_patterns: Verify the target program before invoking CPI
